author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page number below the first page as the first page
summary: Asking for the owner listing at page zero or below currently reaches the error page. It must list the first page of owners instead, leaving every other listing behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: given the owner listing asked for at page zero, when it opens, then the first page of owners is listed rather than the error page
given the owner listing asked for at a page below zero, when it opens, then the first page of owners is listed rather than the error page
given the owner listing asked for at the first page or later, when it opens, then the listing behaves exactly as it does today
non_goals: the veterinarian directory's handling of a page number below the first page — the owner's report named only the owner listing, and the question is recorded in the PRD's Open Questions
page values that are not whole numbers
page numbers beyond the last page of results
notes: Requirement recorded in docs/prd.md under Owner records, anchor req-ownerspageparam-001, with two 'Done when' bullets. Grounded solely in the intake-decision at handoff line 1; its decisions array is empty, so nothing beyond the quoted request is authorized. Non-Goals table untouched, so no scope_overrides apply.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory already covers this unchanged. The owner listing's paged search is the OwnerController row of system-design.md#contracts, and page size is recorded under system-design.md#constants as a local variable in each controller's pagination helper. No new contract, package, dependency, or pattern. Cause located: OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize), and Spring Data's AbstractPageRequest rejects a negative index with IllegalArgumentException, which reaches the error page. The fix is request-parameter normalization at the existing web boundary. Basis is grep plus a full read of OwnerController.java and templates/owners/ownersList.html; no IDE oracle was connected in this run, so this is the weaker resolution basis.
integration_points: GET /owners request parameter 'page' bound by @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page in OwnerController.processFindForm
the normalized page value feeds both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (the PageRequest index) and addPaginationModel (the currentPage model attribute)

patterns.description: external input arrives at the controller: validate type, range, and shape before use. REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 widens the accepted contract rather than the rejection: any value below the first page is defined as the first page, so the boundary normalizes instead of rejecting. The boundary check is not weakened, it is restated

the Web controller row admits binding the request and delegating, and holds no business rule. Clamping a paging parameter to the range the query accepts is request binding, not a business rule, so it does not trip the fresh-violation clause at architecture-principles.md:91. Record this reading if a reviewer questions the placement
the identical pagination helper shape in the vet feature, which the PRD holds out of scope

risks.risk: normalizing only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName leaves the raw page value in the model, so currentPage renders as 0 or negative and templates/owners/ownersList.html mis-renders the navigation: no page is marked current because currentPage != i holds for every i, and the first/previous controls key off currentPage > 1
risks.mitigation: normalize once at the entry of processFindForm so the query index and the currentPage model attribute derive from the same value

risks.risk: VetController.findPaginated carries the same PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) shape, so /vets.html?page=0 still renders the error page after this slice lands
risks.mitigation: out of scope by the prd-entry non_goals; the PRD Open Questions already carries whether the rule binds the veterinarian directory. Do not touch VetController in this slice

notes: No writes to docs/ from this triage. This defect is absent from system-design.md#known-defects and stays absent: that table records behaviors that remain in the code, and this one is being fixed. After the slice lands, the owner listing and the vet directory diverge in their handling of a page below the first; the divergence is already tracked as a PRD Open Question, so no ADR is warranted yet. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: requestedPageIndex() is named and used as a pure query (assertThat(requestedPageIndex(), is(0))) but its body calls verify(this.owners)..., which is itself an assertion with a side effect: a mismatched invocation count throws a MockitoException from inside what reads as a getter. A future reader calling this helper a second time, or reading the assertion failure, will not expect a verification failure to originate from a value accessor. This violates the project's 'no side effects in methods named as queries' guideline.
findings.fix: Split the two responsibilities: verify the interaction once (verify(this.owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), pageable.capture())) inline in each test right after the mockMvc.perform(...) call, or rename the helper to something that discloses the verification, e.g. verifyRequestedPageIndex(), so its name matches what it does.

findings.description: The new private helper requestedPageIndex() is inserted between two @Test methods (theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenPageIsNegative at line 166 and processFindFormByLastName at line 190), breaking the file's existing convention of keeping helpers (george() at line 75) grouped away from the list of @Test methods. A reader scanning down the class for the test roster now has to step over a non-test method mid-list.
findings.fix: Move requestedPageIndex() next to the george() fixture helper near the top of the class, or to the bottom of the class after the last @Test method.

approved_aspects: FIRST_PAGE constant and Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) clamp read clearly and match the design-block's normalize-once-at-entry guidance

requestedPage is computed once in processFindForm and threaded through both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so the query index and the currentPage model attribute stay in sync as the design-block's risk note required
checkFormat passes cleanly on the diff (verified with --rerun-tasks)
New tests follow the existing PageImpl/MockMvc idioms in the file and the BDD test names match the prd-entry's test_names

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Class sweep for 'request-derived page param reaching PageRequest.of' found exactly two instances repo-wide: OwnerController (fixed here) and VetController:45/61 (`/vets.html`), which still throws on `page=0` and still wraps on `page=-2147483648`. VetController is outside this change set and is pre-existing baseline, so it is not a finding under docs/security-principles.md ('pre-existing absences in that baseline are never findings') - and the diff already raises it as a PRD open question. Flagging it only so the answer to that question is not lost: the same one-line clamp closes the same overflow there.

Depth-in-place option, not a defect: findPaginatedForOwnersLastName(int page, ...) still accepts an unclamped int and performs `page - 1` itself. Every current caller passes the clamped value, so there is no reachable path today; moving the clamp into that private method (or asserting the precondition there) would make the invariant local to the arithmetic that depends on it and survive a future second caller.

Supply chain was NOT verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependencyCheck plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins block carries spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11), and this reviewer has no network access. No dependency changed in this diff, so the risk delta is zero, but the standing CVE check on Spring Boot 4.1.0 and the resolved Jackson version remains open for CI or a human. The project does publish a CycloneDX SBOM, which is the natural feed for that check.
approved_aspects: Boundary validation strengthened: the request-derived `page` param is now clamped at the handler boundary (OwnerController.processFindForm:99) before it reaches PageRequest.of, which is where docs/security-principles.md puts defensive checks ('Validate type, range, and shape before use').

Removes an unhandled-exception path rather than adding one: previously `GET /owners?page=0` reached `PageRequest.of(-1, 5)`, which throws IllegalArgumentException and renders the error page. Per docs/security-principles.md the error page renders the underlying exception message, so eliminating an attacker-triggerable exception narrows an internal-detail disclosure surface.

Integer-overflow path closed: `page=-2147483648` previously computed `page - 1` as Integer.MAX_VALUE (silent wraparound), producing a ~10.7-billion-row offset query from a single unauthenticated GET. Math.max clamps before the subtraction, so the arithmetic can no longer wrap.
No unbounded-resource risk on the upper end: a large `page` yields an empty Page, which routes to the existing `notFound` rejection path rather than allocating per the requested index.

No new attack surface: no new endpoint, no new request-bound field, no change to mass-assignment disallow lists, no template or escaping change. `currentPage` is an int, so the new model attribute carries no request-derived text into the rendered page.
No supply-chain delta: build.gradle is unchanged, so no dependency was added and the four-check dependency policy in system-design.md is not engaged.
No secrets, credentials, logging, file I/O, shell execution, deserialization, or query-string concatenation introduced; data access stays on the derived repository query `findByLastNameStartingWith`.
Thread safety holds: FIRST_PAGE is a static final int and requestedPage is a method local, so the singleton controller gains no mutable shared state.

Test additions are read-only MockMvc exercises with no credentials or external I/O; the ArgumentCaptor assertion pins the actual zero-based index sent to the repository, which is the evidence that the clamp reached the query and not just the view model.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The two new tests introduce a standalone (non-MockMvc-DSL) assertion via `org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert.assertThat(requestedPageIndex(), is(0))`. This is new code, so testing-principles.md's assertion rule (`docs/testing-principles.md` Assertions section) and CLAUDE.md's 'JUnit 5 and AssertJ' stack binding apply: prefer fluent AssertJ. Every other file in the suite that does a standalone assertThat (e.g. PetTypeFormatterTests.java) already uses `org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat(...).isEqualTo(...)`; OwnerControllerTests.java is the only file using Hamcrest's MatcherAssert for a bare assertion, and only because these two new tests just introduced it — it is not a pre-existing host-file convention being matched.
findings.fix: Replace `import static org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert.assertThat;` and the two call sites with `import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;` and `assertThat(requestedPageIndex()).isEqualTo(0);`. (The MockMvc `andExpect(...)` matchers elsewhere in the file are the sanctioned Hamcrest usage baked into Spring's MockMvc DSL and are unaffected.)

findings.description: theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenPageIsZero and theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenPageIsNegative are copy-paste duplicates differing only in the requested `page` query value (0 vs -3); both assert the identical outcome (currentPage=1, requestedPageIndex=0). testing-principles.md's Common Issues list names this pattern directly: 'Missing @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases' is an autofix-class finding.
findings.fix: Collapse the two tests into one @ParameterizedTest (e.g. @ValueSource(ints = {0, -3}) or @CsvSource) named to cover 'a page at or below the first page', keeping the two acceptance-criteria values (0 and a representative negative) as the data points.

approved_aspects: Both new tests are named per the BDD school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`) and match the PRD's prescribed test_names exactly

requestedPageIndex() correctly asserts the actual root-cause behavior (the zero-based PageRequest index sent to the repository), not just the surface HTTP status, catching a regression to the pre-fix off-by-one/negative-index defect
The currentPage model attribute assertion covers the design-block's identified pagination-template risk (raw vs. normalized page value diverging)
./gradlew test passes; no regressions in the existing OwnerControllerTests suite

PRD acceptance criteria for page=0 and page<0 are each covered by a dedicated test; the third criterion (page>=1 unaffected) is covered by the pre-existing, unmodified processFindFormSuccess/processFindFormByLastName tests exercising page=1
Four-phase structure with blank-line separation is followed, consistent with the host file
